topic: Power iteration for dominant vibration modes in second-year mechanical engineering

entry_point.discipline_context: Mechanical engineers often need the dominant vibration mode of a structure to predict resonance and design safer systems.
entry_point.rationale: Starting from a simple mass-spring analogy makes eigenvalues and eigenvectors concrete before the numerical iteration is introduced.
entry_point.analogy_boundary: The structural vibration analogy is helpful for intuition, but the iteration itself is the same linear algebra method used for any square matrix.

chapter_sequence.title: From vibration modes to eigenvalue problems
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce eigenvalues and eigenvectors as the mathematical language of free vibration and modal analysis.

chapter_sequence.title: Why the dominant mode matters
chapter_sequence.purpose: Explain the role of the largest-magnitude eigenvalue and the meaning of a dominant vibration mode.

chapter_sequence.title: Power iteration as a repeated vibration update
chapter_sequence.purpose: Present the update rule, normalisation, and the intuition behind repeated matrix-vector products.

chapter_sequence.title: Estimating the modal frequency and checking the approximation
chapter_sequence.purpose: Introduce the Rayleigh quotient and residual as practical measures of quality.

chapter_sequence.title: Python implementation and exercises
chapter_sequence.purpose: Show a readable NumPy implementation and provide exercises that connect the mathematics to code and vibration interpretation.

implementation_strategy: Use a compact symmetric 2x2 matrix example and a short NumPy implementation so the code remains readable and directly connected to the vibration interpretation.
assessment_strategy: Provide 6 exercises that test the definition of eigenpairs, the role of the dominant mode, the stopping criterion, and simple implementation choices.
